stages.name: Trade liberalisation and protectionism
stages.title: Trade liberalisation and protectionism
stages.sub: You can weigh up the advantages of opening an economy to trade against the disadvantages of shielding it.

steps.q: A country that used to make everything itself now focuses only on the crops it grows best, buying other goods from abroad instead. What tends to happen to how efficiently its resources are used?
steps.right: Efficiency rises, since resources go to what the country does best
steps.wrong: Efficiency falls, since the country now relies on others
steps.hint: Think about what happens when workers and land stop being spread across everything and are focused on one strength.

steps.q: A government instead puts high taxes on imports to protect its own firms from foreign competition. If those firms face no pressure to cut costs or improve, and consumers can only buy from them, what happens to prices, choice and innovation at home?
steps.right: Prices rise, choice shrinks and firms have less reason to innovate
steps.wrong: Prices fall, choice grows and firms innovate faster
steps.hint: Without foreign rivals pushing them, why would domestic firms bother to improve or compete on price?

steps.q: A shoe factory that once sold only to its home market now sells to customers worldwide. Can it now produce a much larger quantity, spreading its costs over more units?
steps.right: Yes, larger output lets average costs per unit fall
steps.wrong: No, average costs per unit stay the same regardless of output
steps.hint: Think about a factory building 10,000 pairs of shoes a year against one building 10 million. Does cost per pair change?

steps.q: Removing taxes on imported goods means a family can now buy the same imported rice for less money than before. Does their money now buy them more, or the same as before?
steps.right: More, since the same wage now buys more goods
steps.wrong: The same, since their wage in money terms has not changed
steps.hint: Their pay in pounds or dollars hasn't risen, but does that mean nothing has changed for what they can afford?

steps.prompt: Drag and drop the 4 key terms in the order they build on each other.

steps.q: A country has just set up its first car manufacturer. If it removes all import taxes immediately, this new firm must compete straight away with huge, experienced foreign carmakers. Is it likely to survive?
steps.right: No, it is likely to be driven out before it can grow
steps.wrong: Yes, since consumers will still choose the cheapest cars available
steps.hint: Think about a brand new small firm going head to head with giant, established foreign competitors from day one.
